clue.text: Looks over pages showing spices

indicators.note: the word for looks is laid over, i.e. wrapped around, the pages abbreviation

parts.note: to look closely is to peer, so looks gives peers

explanation.surface: Someone flips through a cookbook's pages to find the right spices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' works as a container signal here: the word for looks sits over, i.e. wraps, the abbreviation for pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Peppercorns and chillies are both seasonings, so the plural names a kind of spice.

clue.text: 22, as in twice eleven, for a start? Right

indicators.note: in places the word as inside the doubled pair of letters
twice says the two-letter piece built from eleven and right is written out two times
for a start asks for only the opening letter of the word eleven

explanation.surface: A puzzle about the number twenty-two, written as two elevens, asks whether that is right.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer to 22, RUBBER. E (first of eleven) plus R, doubled, gives ERER, and AS goes in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: In British English a rubber is the everyday word for a pencil-mark remover.

clue.text: Having a good record as a boxer, say

definitions.text: Having a good record as a boxer, say

parts.words: Having a good record as a boxer, say
parts.note: the surface suggests a prizefighter's winning record, but the record meant is a dog's documented breeding line, the boxer being a dog breed

explanation.surface: A fighter with an impressive record of wins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' is the breed of dog, not a fighter; the 'good record' is a registered family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog with a registered line of descent from recognised ancestors has papers proving its breeding.

clue.text: Pot-smoker spotted in orchestra stalls

indicators.note: spotted in means the letters can be seen sitting inside the run of words orchestra stalls

explanation.surface: Someone smoking cannabis is noticed among the audience in the stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across orchestRA STAlls.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of the Rastafarian movement are known for ritual cannabis use.

clue.text: Try another case, perhaps, concerning collection of suits

parts.note: RE means about or concerning, as in a letter heading
a pack of cards is made up of four suits

explanation.surface: A lawyer considers a fresh case involving a set of business suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks legal and 'suits' looks like clothing or lawsuits, but it is a suitcase and playing-card suits.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things into a different suitcase or box is to fill a container again.

clue.text: Tree, by the way, making excellent prize

parts.note: royal can mean splendid or first-rate, as in a royal welcome
the palm is the traditional token of victory, so it means a prize

explanation.surface: An aside about a tree winning a top award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like a throwaway aside but belongs to the definition: these trees famously line avenues and roads.
explanation.definitionFit: This tall Caribbean palm species is widely planted along boulevards and driveways.

clue.text: Bird holding bill up to get nut

indicators.note: holding means the bird's letters wrap around the other piece

parts.note: a pen is a female swan

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for bill is written from bottom to top

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill

explanation.surface: A bird tilts its beak upward to grab a nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a beak but is an account; in a down entry 'up' reads it bottom to top. The stray letters in the stored clue are OCR noise from the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This North American hardwood tree yields a sweet edible kernel used in pies.

clue.text: Dumb thing like this? Not so

parts.note: the item being read is a crossword clue, so this self-reference gives clue
less means not so much, as in less heavy

explanation.surface: Someone calls this clue stupid and is contradicted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thing like this' points at the clue you are reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone without any idea is stupid or ignorant, a colloquial sense of dumb.

clue.text: It may be painfully necessary, following oral examination

definitions.text: It may be painfully necessary, following oral examination

parts.words: It may be painfully necessary, following oral examination
parts.note: the surface hints at a student's spoken exam, but the oral examination is a check-up of the mouth, after which a tool may be needed to treat decay

explanation.surface: After a viva, something unpleasant may have to follow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral examination' sounds academic; it is a check-up at the dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist uses a high-speed rotary tool to remove decay found during a check-up.

clue.text: See 22
Disreputable record wrongly stressed, we hear

indicators.note: the letters said aloud are stressed on the first syllable instead of the second, which turns them into another word
we hear signals that the clue works by sound

parts.note: a CD is a compact disc, a record

explanation.surface: A shady record has had its emphasis put in the wrong place.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, CD is 'see-DEE'; move the stress to the front and you hear 'SEE-dy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A shabby, sleazy place or person has a bad reputation.

clue.text: Arsenal, for example, provides this weapon

definitions.meaning: Arsenal is a London football team, an example of a sports organisation
a heavy stick used for hitting is a simple arm

explanation.surface: A gun store supplies a particular weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arsenal' looks like a weapons store but is the London football team.
explanation.definitionFit: A sports team is a members' organisation, and a cudgel is a blunt hitting weapon.

clue.text: Officer material leading soldier, perhaps

indicators.note: leading says the fabric word comes in front of the other piece

parts.note: serge is a hard-wearing woollen fabric
a soldier ant is one caste of ant, so a soldier may be an ant

explanation.surface: Good officer material is someone who could lead soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' sounds like potential, but it is cloth; 'soldier' is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-commissioned rank in the army or police above corporal.

clue.text: Lacking company, running into Dutch artist in England

indicators.note: into says the running word goes inside the artist's name

parts.note: Sir Peter Lely was a Dutch-born painter who worked at the English court
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A painter from Holland working in England feels isolated.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Lely painted at the Stuart court, which is why the clue adds 'in England' to 'Dutch artist'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without companions means being solitary and isolated.

clue.text: Assist with it, putting in pound

indicators.note: putting in says the pound symbol is placed inside the slang word

parts.note: hep is old slang for fashionable or with it, like hip
L, from Latin libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: Someone offers to help and chips in a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with it' looks like a link phrase but is slang for trendy, HEP.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid someone is to give them support.

clue.text: General reviews soldiers in hats

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the hats

parts.note: Panamas are lightweight straw hats
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A general inspects troops wearing hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'General' looks like an army officer but is an adjective: broad surveys.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-ranging survey of a subject is a comprehensive overview.

clue.text: Badly held back by accident? Not to any great extent

indicators.note: held says the crash word holds the reversed piece inside it

parts.note: a smash is a collision or crash

indicators.note: back says the word for badly is written right to left

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: Someone was badly delayed by a crash, though not seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held back' reads as delayed, but 'back' turns ILL into LLI, held by SMASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairly little in size or degree, somewhat small.

clue.text: Wrongly alleged one's D M R A breaking in — no longer DISOWNE ID criminal

annotationWithheld.why: Held as 'Wrongly alleged one's D M R A breaking in — no longer DISOWNE ID criminal': stray OCR text inside the clue, no scan to confirm the printed wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Wrongly alleged one's D M R A breaking in — no longer DISOWNE ID criminal

clue.text: E.g. mostly butter spread over a loaf

indicators.note: spread signals that the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the abbreviation are used as written

indicators.note: mostly drops the final letter of butter

explanation.surface: Butter is spread over a loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: EG, BUTTE (butter less its last letter) and A are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A long thin French stick of bread is a kind of loaf.

clue.text: Game fish

definitions.meaning: a party game in which one player hides and the others squeeze into the hiding place
small oily sea fish often sold in tins

explanation.surface: Fish caught for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's hide-and-seek variant takes its name from tinned pilchards, which are also small edible fish.

clue.text: Old woman battling American wise guys

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old woman
a GI is an American soldier, a fighting American

explanation.surface: An elderly woman fights an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wise guys' sounds like smart alecs but means the Wise Men of the Nativity.
explanation.definitionFit: The three learned visitors from the East in the Nativity story are known as the Wise Men.

clue.text: Kind of ticket that makes a profit

definitions.meaning: a ticket covering the journey there and back
the gain or yield on an investment

explanation.surface: A lucrative sort of ticket.
explanation.definitionFit: A round-trip fare is one sense; the yield from an investment is the other.

clue.text: Some bridge players used to secure a lot of money, say

definitions.text: used to secure a lot of money, say

parts.note: a rubber is a set of games in bridge
a band is a group of musicians, players

explanation.surface: A group of card players use it to guard their winnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bridge' is the card game and 'players' are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastic loop is used to hold a wad of banknotes together.

clue.text: Aristocrat as young man meeting a queen

parts.note: a boy is a young male
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A nobleman, as a youth, meets the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOYAR was a member of the old Russian nobility.
explanation.definitionFit: Boyars were the highest-ranking nobles in medieval Russia.

clue.text: Devotee turned over extremely limited weapon

indicators.note: turned over says the devotee word is written backwards

parts.note: a lover is a devotee, an enthusiast

indicators.note: limited means the word for extremely is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: very means extremely

explanation.surface: A fan flips over a weapon of very limited power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely limited' looks like one phrase, but VERY (extremely) is limited to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun with a rotating cylinder of chambers is a kind of gun.

clue.text: Visionary Frenchman governed with divine protection

indicators.note: protection means the divine being wraps around the answer inside governed, so taking those letters away leaves what was protected

parts.note: god is a divine being

explanation.surface: A far-sighted French leader rules under the shield of heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'governed with divine protection' as a word that has a deity wrapped round it: strip that protecting deity's letters and the novelist is what was inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne, the French novelist, foresaw submarines and space travel in his fiction.

clue.text: Guy last in race

definitions.meaning: a guy is a rope holding a tent or mast steady
to keep going to the finish of a race, to endure

explanation.surface: A man finishes at the back of the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' is the verb endure, not the final place.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporting rope on a ship is one sense; to keep going in a race is the other.

clue.text: Competitor in event for forty-two ponies

annotationWithheld.why: Competitor in event for forty-two ponies (5): 'forty-two ponies' gives no sense for MILER as held and no source confirms the printed wording
annotationWithheld.clue: Competitor in event for forty-two ponies

clue.text: Single listened to for a kind of music

indicators.note: listened to signals that the clue works by sound

parts.note: sole means only or single

explanation.surface: A hit single heard on the radio for one style of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' suggests a record, but it is the adjective, SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A genre of African-American popular music rooted in gospel and rhythm and blues.

clue.text: Football club getting 50% of the red cards

definitions.meaning: Heart of Midlothian is an Edinburgh football club, known by this nickname
of the two red suits in a pack, one is this suit

explanation.surface: A football team gets half its players sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red cards' look like football dismissals but are the red playing cards, diamonds and the other red suit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edinburgh club Heart of Midlothian is commonly called this; it is also one of the two red suits.

clue.text: Studying in university town? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.text: university town? Doesn't sound like it
definitions.meaning: a Berkshire town with a university, whose name is spelt like the verb but pronounced 'redding'

explanation.surface: A student in a university town is told their name sounds wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The Berkshire town of Reading, west of London, is pronounced 'redding', not like the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: British students read a subject, meaning study it; the Berkshire town has a university.
